understanding how insulin and other hormones regulate metabolism, and how these processes are disrupted in disease.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we study the molecular basis of insulin action in health and disease, with the aim of understanding how the body responds to excess nutrients, and how this response is altered by genetic and environmental factors.
we have been studying the mechanisms of insulin action, in the context of insulin resistance, in order to understand the pathophysiology of type 2 Diabetes.
we have been investigating the role of the insulin receptor and the insulin signalling pathway in the regulation of glucose homeostasis, and the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetic states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insulin signalling is highly integrated with many other signalling systems in the body, and that the regulation of insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism is a complex and highly dynamic process.
the insulin receptor is the master regulator of glucose and lipid homeostasis.
the signalling pathways that control insulin action are not as simple as once thought, and that many other hormones, including leptin, adiponectin and ghrelin, can influence insulin action.
